diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), Not Otherwise Specified (NOS)
stage: Ann Arbor Stage IV (Lugano Stage IV) with B symptoms (night sweats, weight loss)

biology.cell_of_origin: Germinal Center B-cell-like (GCB) subtype (CD20+, CD10+, BCL6+, MUM1- by Hans algorithm)
biology.double_hit_triple_hit: Negative (FISH negative for MYC, BCL2, and BCL6 rearrangements)
biology.double_expressor: Negative (BCL2 30% and MYC 20%, both below conventional thresholds of >=50% and >=40%)

prognosis.score_calculation: Age >60 (1 pt), Stage IV (1 pt), ECOG 2 (1 pt), Elevated LDH (1 pt), >1 extranodal site (1 pt) -> Total IPI Score: 5 (High Risk)
prognosis.estimated_outcomes: High-risk DLBCL with an IPI score of 5 has an estimated 5-year overall survival of approximately 50-55%.

first_line_treatment: R-CHOP (Rituximab, Cyclophosphamide, Doxorubicin, Vincristine, Prednisone) for 6 cycles, or Pola-R-CHP (Polatuzumab vedotin, Rituximab, Cyclophosphamide, Doxorubicin, Prednisone) for 6 cycles (supported by the POLARIX trial for intermediate/high-risk DLBCL).

cns_risk.cns_ipi_score: CNS-IPI Score: 5 (High Risk) based on age >60, Stage III/IV, elevated LDH, ECOG >1, and high-risk extranodal involvement (renal and adrenal glands).
cns_risk.prophylaxis_recommendation: CNS-directed prophylaxis (e.g., systemic high-dose methotrexate or intrathecal chemotherapy) should be considered given high CNS-IPI risk and high-risk extranodal sites (kidney/adrenal), though survival benefit remains debated.
cns_risk.uncertainty: Optimal prophylaxis strategy remains controversial in DLBCL without baseline CNS involvement.

response_assessment.timing: End of treatment (after completion of 6 cycles of systemic therapy)
response_assessment.criteria: Lugano 2014 classification utilizing the Deauville 5-Point Scale (Scores 1-3 defined as Complete Metabolic Response).

missing_information: Hepatitis B serologies (HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs) and Hepatitis C antibody (mandatory prior to anti-CD20 therapy)
Baseline cardiac ejection fraction assessment (Echocardiogram or MUGA scan) prior to anthracycline exposure
Baseline cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis (cytology and flow cytometry) and brain MRI to rule out occult CNS involvement
Baseline uric acid and comprehensive metabolic panel for tumor lysis syndrome risk stratification
